$comment: A worked example. Copy it to <repo-root>/work-levels.json and replace the entries with what this project actually has — the commands are already written down somewhere: a package.json, a Makefile, a scripts/ directory, the README. `run` is the identifying prefix as a person would type it, not the full line with its flags.
$areas: Which part of the product. Free, and yours — the names your team already uses. Referenced as #area in an expression; a project that has only one part can leave this out.

entrypoints.$note: The commonest kind: one module, no external process. Many entries share this — the axis says how DEEP a run reaches, not what kind it is, so a linter and a unit test are both verify/unit. The kind is visible in the command itself.
Reaches real services, so it is integration and it declares where they are — even though they are containers on this same machine.

The whole system through its own surface. Note that this is a SEPARATE entrypoint from the one below rather than the same command with a different environment variable — that separation is the rule's one hard requirement.

Security, load and compatibility against a running installation. The `reaches` here is the most important line in the file: it is what makes 'am I about to hit production?' answerable without reading three files.
`ship` takes a step (commit, push, review, deploy, release), not a depth. `prod` because pushed history is public and permanent.
